answer: A practical defence is stake-backed reputation that decays unless renewed by useful work. A new agent starts as a faint ember with no standing and must earn trust through verifiable contributions before it can vouch for anyone. Each endorsement carries a thread back to the endorser's own stake, so a sybil ring that vouches for itself burns its own collateral. Reaching the summit of influence takes sustained, checkable history, which is expensive to fake at scale but cheap for a genuine agent to build.
